Our team at Blackline Safety is growing! As a people-driven technology company, with a mission to make sure every worker returns home safely, we drive innovation, practice resiliency, demonstrate leadership, go the extra mile for our customers, and empower our people to be their best. 
 Blackline Safety is currently hiring skilled Electronics Assemblers to perform a variety of assembly tasks including soldering, test, assembly and packaging. This role reports to our facility in Calgary, Alberta and is not remote. 
 Key Responsibilities 
 1. Component Assembly:
 Assemble electronic components and sub-assemblies according to engineering drawings, specifications, and work instructions.
 Use precision hand tools, soldering irons, and other equipment to perform intricate assembly tasks.
 2. Soldering and Wiring:
 Perform soldering tasks to connect and secure electronic components on printed circuit boards (PCBs).
 Follow wiring diagrams and instructions to connect and route wires and cables within electronic assemblies.
 3. Quality Control:
 Conduct visual inspections of components and finished assemblies to ensure adherence to quality standards.
 Identify and rectify any defects or discrepancies during the assembly process.
 4. Testing and Troubleshooting:
 Conduct functional tests on completed electronic assemblies.
 Collaborate with quality assurance teams to troubleshoot and resolve any issues identified during testing.
 5. Documentation:
 Maintain accurate records of assembly processes, configurations, and test results.
 Complete production and quality control documentation as required.
 6. Material Handling:
 Manage and organize electronic components, ensuring proper storage and inventory control.
 Notify supervisors of any shortages or discrepancies in materials.
 7. Workstation Maintenance:
 Keep workstations clean, organized, and equipped with necessary tools and materials.
 Report any equipment malfunctions or maintenance needs promptly.
 8. Adherence to Safety Standards:
 Follow safety protocols and guidelines to ensure a safe working environment.
 Report any safety concerns or incidents to supervisors.
 9. Collaboration:
 Work collaboratively with team members and other departments to meet production goals and timelines.
 About You   
 High school diploma or equivalent; additional technical certifications in electronics assembly is a plus.
 Proven experience in electronic assembly, soldering, and component integration.
 Familiarity with reading and interpreting engineering drawings and schematics.
 Attention to detail and precision in manual assembly tasks.
 Proficiency in using hand tools, soldering equipment, and other assembly tools.
 Basic understanding of electronic components and their functions.
 Ability to work in a team-based manufacturing environment.
 Excellent time management skills to meet production deadlines.
 Ability to stand for extended periods in a production or manufacturing environment.
 Required Footwear 
 Safety Shoe Requirement: This position requires the use of CSA Grade 1 toe protection safety footwear. Applicants must have access to a pair of safety footwear that meets this requirement prior to starting employment.
 Total Rewards  
 At Blackline Safety, we offer more than just a job—we offer a career with purpose. Our Total Rewards offerings are designed to support the diverse needs of our global workforce and vary based on employment type and location. They may include: 
 Competitive base salary and annual compensation review 
 Comprehensive health and dental benefits* 
 Mental health and wellness support 
 Flexible work arrangements and hybrid work model for eligible positions 
 Paid vacation, personal and sick days* 
 Professional development opportunities 
 Education funding  
 A collaborative, inclusive, and mission-driven culture  
 Exclusive access to perks and discounts  
 A flexible ‘Dress for Your Day’ environment 
 *Eligibility and coverage vary by employment type and region.  
 Diversity, Equity & Inclusion  
 Blackline Safety is powered by the diversity of our talented employees. We are an equal opportunity employer. We consider all applicants, regardless of age, religion, race, color, ancestry, gender, gender identity or expression, disability, national origin, race, or sexual orientation. We enthusiastically encourage all individuals to apply for positions that fit their passions.
 If you require accommodation during the recruitment process, please contact us at careers@blacklinesafety.com. We are committed to ensuring an accessible and equitable experience for all candidates. 
 Join Us  
 If you’re passionate about technology, safety, and making a difference, we’d love to hear from you. Apply today and help us build a safer, more connected world. 
 Unauthorized Recruitment Communication Alert  
 We are aware of the instances in which individuals are receiving fraudulent job offers or interview requests that are fraudulently alleged to be from Blackline Safety. 
 Blackline Safety does not request payment or personal financial information at any stage of the recruitment process.
 Please exercise caution, and do not respond to emails or other communications that are not from a Blackline Safety email address.

Who we are 
 Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale. 
 Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term. 
 Recovering entrepreneur? Frustrated with bureaucracy? Want to write the roadmap, not inherit one? 
 We're hiring across multiple levels and verticals. The nice thing about growing 30%+ at ~$2B ARR is that we need great engineers everywhere, and we have the room to shape the role around the right person. You build like a founder. We give you the platform to do it at scale.
 About the role: 
 Samsara (NYSE: IOT) sits at the center of hardware, software, AI, and the physical world. The platform processes 25+ trillion data points annually from IoT sensors, cameras, and connected devices across thousands of organizations, and that dataset is compounding: it grew from 4 trillion to 25+ trillion in four years. We're still early in turning that data into the products that will define how physical operations run, and we're hiring the engineers who will build what comes next.
 We're approaching ~$2B ARR growing 30%+ year over year, with 96% of our largest customers on two or more products. The fastest-growing divisions at Samsara are tackling the hardest, most ambiguous problems at the company: building new products from scratch, applying AI and ML to massive real-world datasets, and shipping capabilities that change how organizations maintain equipment, manage fleets, and run day-to-day operations. Most of this work is zero-to-one, at billion-dollar scale.
 We're looking for software engineers who want to define what ships next. Leveling is broad and flexible: we're hiring from Senior through Staff+, across platform and product, and we're open to shaping scope around the right person's strengths and interests. That window won't stay open long.
 This role is remote and open to candidates residing in Canada. Relocation assistance will not be provided for this role. 
 You should apply if: 
 You want to impact the industries that run our world. The software you build will have real-world stakes: helping keep the lights on, getting food into grocery stores, keeping workers safe. What ships here isn't metrics on a dashboard. It shows up on the loading dock, the job site, and the dispatch floor.
 You want to build, not maintain. Samsara is in full growth mode. We're building new systems from scratch, not babysitting old ones. You'd own entire problem spaces end to end, with the autonomy to set direction from day one.
 You want to work where AI meets the physical world. Samsara has spent a decade building the largest proprietary dataset for physical operations. More connected assets generate more data, more data trains better models, better models drive more value, and more value wins more assets. The market and the opportunity here are what set us apart, not just the models.
 You believe customers are more than a number. Samsara engineers have a rare closeness to end users. You'll participate in customer interviews, collaborate with product managers and customer success, and use that context to build products that solve real problems operators face every day.
 You have the curiosity and drive to figure it out. We're looking for people who take pride in their work and get things done at all costs. The engineers who thrive here don't wait to be told what to build. They define it, ship it, and own the outcome. The rate-limiting step on our teams isn't tooling or process. It's ambition.
 In this role, you will: 
 Take ownership of technically complex, mission-critical areas and run with them. We want to point you in a direction and show up to the demo meeting impressed, not spend our weeks managing the details.
 Define and drive technical strategy for new products and platform capabilities, from backend services and APIs to the customer-facing UI.
 Design and ship full-stack features end to end. You'll work across backend, frontend, and potentially mobile to deliver AI-powered products that solve real operational problems.
 Partner with product, design, and customer-facing teams to translate ambiguous, real-world problems into clear technical plans and measurable outcomes.
 Build and scale the systems behind AI-driven products, including data ingestion, APIs, and the workflows that put intelligence into the hands of operators.
 Raise the bar for the engineers around you through code reviews, design reviews, technical mentorship, and by setting a standard for quality, velocity, and craft.
 Champion, role model, and embed Samsara’s cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale globally and across new offices.
 Minimum requirements for the role: 
 Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or equivalent practical experience.
 8+ years of experience in software design and development, including building and operating production systems at scale.
 Strong full-stack fundamentals. You're comfortable working across backend services, APIs, and frontend (web or mobile) to ship complete products.
 Proficiency in modern languages and frameworks (Go, Python, TypeScript/JavaScript, React, or similar).
 Demonstrated experience leading cross-team or cross-org projects from inception through rollout, including managing ambiguity, driving alignment, and delivering measurable impact.
 Experience building AI-powered or data-driven products. You don't need to train models, but you know how to take AI capabilities and turn them into products customers love.
 Strong communication skills and the ability to translate between technical and non-technical stakeholders.
 A track record of building: zero-to-one products, systems you left in a meaningfully better place, or hard problems you refused to let stay unsolved.
 An ideal candidate also has: 
 Experience shipping AI-powered features in production, whether that's LLM-based products, agentic workflows, recommendation systems, or other customer-facing AI.
 Comfort with modern AI-augmented development workflows (Cursor, LLMs, etc.) to multiply your output and accelerate delivery.
 Background working with real-world operational data (telematics, sensor data, work orders, inspections) or a strong interest in learning the domain.
 A proven track record of mentoring senior engineers and influencing engineering culture, standards, and best practices beyond a single team.
 Side projects, open-source contributions, or other signals of curiosity and drive outside the scope of your day job.
 The compensation range shown spans approved pay zones for this role. Your primary work location determines the range applicable to you, which may be narrower than the full range displayed. 
 The range of annual base salary for full-time employees for this position is below. Please note that base pay offered may vary depending on factors including your city of residence, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. This role is also eligible for an initial RSU grant with no vesting cliff, and ongoing refresh opportunities tied to performance, subject to plan terms and conditions. Learn more about our total rewards and benefits below. 
 Annual Base Salary
 $142,800 — $184,800 CAD 
 Total Rewards 
 At Samsara, we build for the people who keep the global economy moving. We want owners, not passengers, which is why our rewards are designed to fuel high-impact builders. Our compensation program delivers above-market total compensation through a combination of base salary, performance-based bonus/variable pay, and equity (for eligible roles) in a high-growth public company. We meaningfully differentiate pay for our top performers, who have the opportunity to earn above-market compensation that can outpace the broader market over time.
 Beyond compensation, we provide the foundations that enable long-term success: a flexible, employee-led remote model, a professional development stipend, comprehensive health and parental leave plans, and more. If you’re ready to build for the long term and own the outcome, your journey starts here.
 Flexible Working 
 At Samsara, we embrace a flexible working model that caters to the diverse needs of our teams. Our offices are open for those who prefer to work in-person and we also support remote work where it aligns with our operational requirements. For certain positions, being close to one of our offices or within a specific geographic area is important to facilitate collaboration, access to resources, or alignment with our service regions. In these cases, the job description will clearly indicate any working location requirements. Our goal is to ensure that all members of our team can contribute effectively, whether they are working on-site, in a hybrid model, or fully remotely. All offers of employment are contingent upon an individual’s ability to secure and maintain the legal right to work at the company and in the specified work location, if applicable. 
 Belonging at Samsara 
 At Samsara, we welcome everyone regardless of their background. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, and other characteristics protected by law. We depend on the unique approaches of our team members to help us solve complex problems and want to ensure that Samsara is a place where people from all backgrounds can make an impact.
 Accommodations 
 Samsara is an inclusive work environment, and we are committed to ensuring equal opportunity in employment for qualified persons with disabilities. Please email accessibleinterviewing@samsara.com or click here if you require any reasonable accommodations throughout the recruiting process.
 Our Commitment to Authenticity 
 We use Tofu , a fraud detection tool, to validate the authenticity of applications and protect against identity fraud. This ensures we are connecting with real people and allows us to prioritize genuine candidates. Please see Samsara’s Candidate Privacy Notice for more information.
 Fraudulent Employment Offers 
 Samsara is aware of scams involving fake job interviews and offers. Please know we do not charge fees to applicants at any stage of the hiring process. Official communication about your application will only come from emails ending in @samsara.com, @us-greenhouse-mail.io or @mail3.guide.co. For more information regarding fraudulent employment offers, please visit our blog post here .

About Blair Health 
 Blair Health is a clinical infrastructure company closing the specialist gap. Today, someone with perimenopause, menopause, pelvic health, urology or nutrition concerns can see three primary care providers and a specialist and still leave without an answer. Blair changes that.
 Our platform gives generalist clinicians the tools, protocols and clinical support to deliver specialist-grade care across menopause and perimenopause, urology and pelvic health, and nutrition, with weight loss coming soon.
 To date, our focus has been women’s health. We believe all people should have access to specialist-level care, and we are opening our care to men, starting with weight management.
 The Role 
 We’re looking for a commercially minded Internal Medicine or Family Physician to join our clinical leadership team as the Canadian Medical Lead for our weight management vertical. The vertical’s clinical protocols have been developed by our obesity medicine specialist; you’ll provide medical oversight across Canada as we launch and scale, making sure those protocols are delivered safely, consistently and in line with current Canadian guidelines.
 You’ll report to our Chief Medical Officer, Dr. Lindsay Shirreff, and work closely with our obesity medicine specialist, Dr. Pooja Singhal, and our provider group. As Blair Health expands, the role will include involvement in our other verticals.
 Location: Canada, virtual or in person
 Commitment: Part-time, 1–2 days per week
 Reports to: Chief Medical Officer
 What You’ll Do 
 Lead medical oversight of the weight management vertical in Canada, ensuring our established protocols and care pathways are implemented and followed consistently across the provider group.
 Keep protocols current, working with our obesity medicine specialist to review and update them as Canadian guidelines and evidence evolve.
 Lead quality and safety oversight for the vertical, including case reviews, clinical KPI and quality monitoring, and adverse-event review.
 Act as the senior physician resource for our providers, receiving escalations through defined pathways and offering case review, advice and direct consultation where appropriate.
 Take part in clinical leadership meetings and contribute to decisions on clinical governance, provider support and the launch of new services.
 Lead or contribute to education rounds with the provider group.
 Contribute to other verticals as Blair Health expands, including oversight and escalation pathways as new services launch.
 How to Apply 
 Apply through this posting with your CV and a brief note on your weight management and clinical leadership experience.
 Blair Health is committed to equity, diversity, and inclusion. 
 Must Have 
 Licensure and good standing in at least one Canadian province, ideally Ontario
 FRCPC in Internal Medicine or CCFP
 Clinical experience in obesity and weight management, including pharmacotherapy
 CMPA coverage
 Experience or interest in clinical leadership, quality improvement or clinical governance
 Comfort supporting generalist clinicians in a protocol-driven, team-based model, virtually or in person
 Nice to Have 
 Licensure in additional provinces
 French fluency
 Compensation: competitive compensation
 Flexibility: a part-time commitment of 1–2 days per week, virtually or in person
 Leadership: a seat on the clinical leadership team of an early-stage company building clinical infrastructure that closes the specialist gap

WHO ARE WE?

Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company.  We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems.

We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that.

We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft.

We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us!


ROLE OVERVIEW:

As a Business Development Representative (BDR) at Cohere, you will drive revenue growth by identifying, qualifying, and nurturing high-potential leads for our enterprise AI solutions. You’ll act as the first point of contact for prospects, understanding their business needs and aligning them with Cohere’s products to solve complex challenges like natural language processing, AI integration, and scalable language models. You’ll also have the opportunity to sell cutting-edge IP, that is being newly productised, within your own book of business.

 


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:

 - Proactively research and identify target accounts across region in industries such as finance, technology, manufacturing, healthcare, public sector, etc. using tools like LinkedIn Sales Navigator and CRM platforms to prioritise high-fit prospects.

 - Conduct 40+ outbound calls and personalised emails daily to engage decision-makers (e.g., CTOs, CIOs, and Business Unit leads), focusing on understanding their pain points and demonstrating how Cohere’s AI solutions can address them.

 - Qualify leads using the BANT framework (Budget, Authority, Need, Timeline) and document interactions in Salesforce, ensuring a clean and actionable pipeline for the sales team.

 - Collaborate with marketing to refine messaging and campaigns based on prospect feedback, contributing to a 15%+ improvement in campaign response rates.

 - Stay updated on industry trends, competitor offerings, and Cohere’s product roadmap to position our solutions effectively and anticipate customer needs.

 - Run independent sales cycles on smaller opportunities with less overhead, from intro to close.


QUALIFICATIONS:

 - 2+ years of experience in business development, sales, or a related role, with a proven track record of exceeding lead generation targets in a SaaS or tech environment.

 - Strong communication skills, with the ability to articulate complex technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders and build rapport quickly over phone and email.

 - Familiarity with CRM tools (e.g., Salesforce, HubSpot) and sales enablement platforms, with the ability to analyse data to optimize outreach strategies.

 - Experience in AI, machine learning, or enterprise software sales, with a basic understanding of natural language processing (NLP) concepts.

 - Closing experience is seen as an advantage.

 - A builder mindset is necessary to succeed here, the challenges will be unique based on the team you’ll be working with, and the role will evolve over time.




FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES AT COHERE ENJOY THESE PERKS:

 - A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch.

 - Full health and dental benefits, including a separate budget for mental health.

 - RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme.

 - 100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent.

 - Annual enrichment benefits:
   
   Arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, and a workspace improvement credit.
   
   Education & learning stipend for conferences, courses, and coaching.

 - 6 weeks of paid vacation (30 working days!)

 - Budget for traveling to other offices if you are remote, plus an annual company offsite.




HOW AND WHERE WE WORK:

 - Cohere is remote-friendly, but we also have offices in Toronto, London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul with more opening soon.

 - For those in the office: a daily lunch program, plenty of snacks, and regular community and social events.

 - For those not near an office: a co-working benefit so you can work alongside others in your city.

 - Everyone receives a $500 home office stipend to set up your workspace properly.
   
   

If any of the above doesn’t line up exactly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply.

CAN YOU TURN POWERFUL PRODUCT CAPABILITIES INTO A REAL REASON FOR SERVICE BUSINESSES TO SWITCH?



Then Jobber might be the place for you! We're looking for a Product Marketing Manager, Operations to be part of our Product department.

Jobber exists to help people in small businesses be successful. We work with small home service businesses, like your local plumbers, painters, and landscapers, to transform the way service is delivered through technology. With Jobber they can quote, schedule, invoice, and collect payments from their customers while providing an easy and professional customer experience. Running a small business today isn't like it used to be—the way we consume and deliver service is changing rapidly, technology is evolving, and customers expect more. That's why we put the power and flexibility in their hands to run their businesses how, where, and when they want!

Our culture of transparency, inclusivity, collaboration, and innovation has been recognized by Great Place to Work, Canada's Most Admired Corporate Cultures, and more. Jobber has also been named on the Globe and Mail's Canada's Top Growing Companies list, and Deloitte Canada's Technology Fast 50™, Enterprise Fast 15, and Technology Fast 500™ lists. With an Executive team that has over thirty years of industry experience of leading the way, we've come a long way from our first customer in 2011—but we've just scratched the surface of what we want to accomplish for our customers https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EkfZmHrRLx4&list=PLoktA_D-2UEnxMLfCe93bANKXVXd2bdN8&index=24.

The team:

Product Marketing sits within Jobber's Product organization, working alongside product teams to shape how our capabilities go to market and how customers adopt them. You'll join the Operations pillar, which covers the tools customers rely on every day to plan work, coordinate teams, connect the field and office, and understand how their business is performing. As these capabilities evolve, the team helps customers see how they fit together and why Jobber is worth their attention and investment.

The role:

Reporting to the Senior Manager, Product Marketing, the Product Marketing Manager, Operations will lead a defined Operations portfolio, owning positioning, go-to-market strategy and adoption from launch through ongoing learning. You'll start with the customer's business, workflows and challenges, then connect Jobber's capabilities into a clear story, from recognizing a need and choosing the right offering to realizing value through ongoing use. A big part of the challenge is reaching established and scaled businesses in a competitive market, many of which already use another solution, so we're looking for someone who brings creative, evidence-led recommendations on how to reach them, stand out and give them a compelling reason to switch. This is an individual contributor role, and you'll partner closely with your fellow Operations PMMs to connect your portfolio to the broader customer story and pricing and packaging strategy.

The Product Marketing Manager, Operations will:

 - Build a deep understanding of how owners, office teams and field crews plan and complete work, combining customer conversations, competitive insight, win/loss feedback and product data to uncover unmet needs, switching barriers and adoption opportunities.

 - Craft differentiated stories around the customer journey, making the value tangible through product demos, customer proof and clear messaging from discovery through ongoing use.

 - Shape the offer by bringing customer needs, willingness to pay and competitive context into packaging and commercial discussions, and help buyers and customer-facing teams find the right offering for each business.

 - Own the GTM plan for your portfolio with Product and the commercial lead, from target customer and proposition to route to market and success measures, and coordinate readiness with Sales, Enablement, Demand Generation and Lifecycle Marketing.

 - Improve discovery and adoption beyond launch, partnering with Product, Lifecycle Marketing, Education and Customer Success to help customers get started, realize value and build lasting habits.

 - Equip Sales and Success with competitive positioning, customer proof, demos and objection-handling guidance, then bring what you learn about buying barriers back to Product and commercial partners.

 - Keep the story consistent across campaigns, landing pages, product experiences and customer conversations, working with Demand Generation, Web and Lifecycle Marketing.

 - Connect your work to commercial outcomes such as conversion into the right offering, higher-tier attach and meaningful adoption, digging into funnel and cohort data yourself and partnering with Analytics on complex questions.

 - Use AI hands-on for research synthesis, analysis, GTM execution and repeatable workflows, verifying outputs and documenting what works so the whole team can reuse it.

To be successful, you should have:

 - A proven track record in product marketing for software products, including shaping strategy and positioning and owning initiatives through launch and post-launch learning.

 - Strong storytelling and writing skills: you can turn complex functionality into a clear customer benefit and present a recommendation to practitioners and senior stakeholders alike.

 - Sharp commercial judgment: you understand competitive alternatives and switching barriers, and can recommend how to reach an ICP, differentiate an offer and make practical investment trade-offs.

 - Analytical confidence: you can frame a business question, self-serve the data, interpret funnel and cohort evidence, and tell observed results apart from causal claims.

 - Hands-on experience using AI to improve research, GTM execution, analysis or team processes, and the ability to explain the impact and how you verified the work.

 - Experience with SMB software, vertical SaaS, field service or operational workflows is a bonus, and familiarity with home service businesses is helpful.

 - A track record of influencing Product, Sales, Customer Success and Marketing partners without direct authority, with clear ownership and dependable follow-through.

 - Comfort with evolving priorities: you bring recommendations and trade-offs, turn priorities into a practical plan, surface risks early and ask for support when decisions extend beyond your portfolio.

 - Genuine curiosity about how service businesses work, and a drive to learn directly from customers.

 - A collaborative approach that pairs a clear point of view with constructive feedback and respect for others' expertise.

Compensation:

At Jobber, we believe that compensation should be transparent, fair, and reflective of your experience and growth. This role has a minimum annual salary of $98,345, a midpoint of $115,700, and a maximum salary of $133,055, designed to show the progression from learning the ropes to truly excelling.

We design our compensation to reflect each new hire's skills, experience against the complexity of the role, ensuring a fair and competitive salary. Our range is intentionally broad to support growth and long-term impact, with fully established hires typically starting around the midpoint. The higher end of the range is reserved for those who have demonstrated deep expertise and lasting contributions, while offers below the midpoint reflect strong potential with room to develop. This approach ensures that compensation aligns with both an individual's current capabilities and their opportunity for future growth.

Base salary is just one part of a total compensation package that will include equity rewards, annual stipends for health and wellness, retirement savings matching, and an extended health package with fully paid premiums for body and mind. Your professional growth matters to us too! You'll have access to a dedicated talent development program that includes career coaching and opportunities for career development.

We believe in transparency and open conversations about compensation. If you have any questions about our approach, we're happy to discuss them throughout the hiring process!

Location:

We believe great collaboration is intentional, and sometimes that means coming together in person to build, brainstorm, and connect. To support this, the role is open to candidates based in one of our hub cities: Edmonton, Toronto, Vancouver, or Kitchener-Waterloo.

What you can expect from Jobber:

 - A total compensation package that includes an extended health benefits package with fully paid premiums for both body and mind, matching in RRSP, TFSA or FHSA, and stock options.

 - A dedicated Talent Development team and access to coaching, learning, and leadership programs to help you grow your career, reach your goals, and unlock your full potential.

 - A unique opportunity to build, grow, and leave your impact on a $400-billion industry that has no dominant player...yet.

 - To work with a group of people who are humble, supportive, and give a sh*t about our customers.

We believe that diverse teams perform better and that fostering an inclusive work environment is a key part of growing a successful team. We welcome people of diverse backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We are an equal opportunity employer, and we are committed to working with applicants requesting accommodation at any stage of the hiring process.



A bit more about us:

Job by job, we’re transforming the way service is delivered. Your lawn care provider, home cleaning service, plumber or painter could use Jobber to better connect with their customers, save time in the office, invoice faster, and get paid! We’re bringing tens of thousands of people together with technology to deliver billions of dollars a year in services to happy customers. Jobber exists to help make these small businesses successful, and when they’re successful we all win!

 Job Description: 
 Join Us in Shaping the Future
At Intel, we are building the next generation of software technologies that unlock the potential of heterogeneous computing. Our compiler technologies help developers harness CPUs, GPUs, and accelerators through high-performance, portable software. As an intern, you will contribute to an open ecosystem that advances performance, scalability, reliability, and developer productivity for AI, HPC, and other demanding workloads, while supporting Intel's commitment to contributing to and collaborating with open-source communities.
The Team
The Intel Compiler Engineering Team develops LLVM-based C, C++, SYCL, Triton, MLIR, Domain Specific Languages (DSLs), and Fortran compiler technologies for Intel processor platforms, including CPUs and GPUs. The team works across the compiler stack and in close collaboration with hardware architecture teams, covering language front ends, intermediate representations, optimization, code generation, debug information, runtimes, offload support, quality, and developer tooling. This work connects Intel hardware and compiler capabilities with AI frameworks and software ecosystems such as PyTorch, inference engines, and machine-learning models. You will collaborate with experienced engineers and contribute to open-source communities while learning how production compilers are designed, tested, optimized, and delivered.
Position Overview
We are hiring a Compiler Engineer Intern to contribute to Intel's compiler software stack. You will work with experienced compiler and hardware architecture engineers on an engineering or research project that may involve compiler features, MLIR-based intermediate representations, Triton or other Domain Specific Languages (DSLs), optimization, code generation, runtime or offload support, debug information, testing infrastructure, performance analysis, or developer tools. Projects may connect hardware capabilities to AI frameworks such as PyTorch, inference engines such as vLLM and SGLang, and machine-learning model ecosystems such as DeepSeek, Hugging Face, and Qimi. You will investigate technical problems, implement and test solutions, analyze results, and communicate findings to the team. This opportunity is designed for a graduate student who can apply deeper technical expertise to an ambiguous engineering or research problem, evaluate alternatives, and deliver a well-supported solution or prototype.

• Contribute to open-source projects when aligned with the assigned work.

À PROPOS DE CARRUS 
 Carrus conçoit le logiciel de gestion sur lequel les distributeurs de pièces automobiles, les grossistes et les ateliers de réparation de l’Est du Canada s’appuient pour gérer leurs activités — des catalogues électroniques de pièces et de la tarification à l’inventaire, à la facturation et à la comptabilité. Depuis 2002, Carrus sert le marché secondaire de l’automobile avec un logiciel sur lequel ses clients comptent chaque jour au comptoir.
 Carrus est un excellent milieu de travail si vous souhaitez avoir une réelle autonomie sur le fonctionnement d’une équipe et un travail dont les clients ressentent l’impact le jour même. Carrus fait partie de l’écosystème de Valsoft, qui regroupe plus de 150 entreprises de logiciels verticaux, ce qui vous offre la stabilité et les ressources de l’une des entreprises à la croissance la plus rapide au Canada, dans l’ambiance d’une équipe ciblée et tissée serré.
 LE POSTE 
 Nous sommes à la recherche d’un ou d’une chef d’équipe bilingue, Soutien à la clientèle, pour diriger au quotidien l’équipe de soutien de Carrus. Si vous aimez résoudre des problèmes avec les clients au téléphone, accompagner les personnes qui vous entourent et assumer la responsabilité des résultats d’une équipe, ce poste est fait pour vous.
 Vous serez responsable d’améliorer de façon autonome notre système de soutien. Vous travaillerez à cerner et à mettre en œuvre des améliorations aux processus et aux flux de travail afin d’assurer la réactivité de l’équipe et la satisfaction de la clientèle, tout en étant encouragé(e) à automatiser les goulots d’étranglement sans compromettre les normes de service. Vous serez responsable de la formation et du mentorat d’une équipe de service à la clientèle, en l’aidant à améliorer et à prioriser les files d’attente et les flux de travail pour un rendement optimal. Vous apprendrez notre pile technologique et bâtirez des relations avec la clientèle, en étant en mesure de traiter et de résoudre de façon autonome les problèmes et les escalades des clients.
 Vous relèverez du directeur, Produit et Soutien, et travaillerez en étroite collaboration avec les équipes Produit, Développement et Intégration des clients. Vous prendrez en charge les revues quotidiennes de la file d’attente et le suivi des indicateurs de performance clés (IPC) de l’équipe, puis bâtirez le guide de soutien à partir de là : la base de connaissances, les guides d’exploitation, les modèles de réponse ainsi que les flux de travail et les ententes de niveau de service (SLA) dans Jira qui permettent de faire avancer la file d’attente.
 Vous vous épanouirez dans ce rôle si vous restez calme sous pression, prêchez par l’exemple et préférez régler la cause profonde d’un problème plutôt que de résoudre deux fois le même billet. Vous serez évalué(e) selon des indicateurs quantifiables sur lesquels vous avez une influence directe : l’arriéré de billets, le délai moyen de résolution, la satisfaction de la clientèle et les délais de réponse.
 CE QUE VOUS FEREZ 
 Élaborer et améliorer continuellement les processus et les flux de travail de l’organisation en matière de gestion des billets de soutien, de la collecte et du suivi des données clés pour les IPC jusqu’à l’élaboration de guides d’automatisation.
 Accompagner et encadrer une équipe d’agents de soutien sur les pratiques exemplaires afin d’augmenter les taux de résolution des billets et la satisfaction de la clientèle.
 Diriger l’équipe au quotidien — assurer la couverture pendant les heures d’ouverture, animer les rencontres quotidiennes et les rencontres individuelles, et établir et incarner la norme en matière de résolution rapide et rigoureuse.
 Prendre en charge une partie de la file de billets, particulièrement les problèmes hautement prioritaires — répondre aux appels et aux demandes entrants en français et en anglais.
 Trier et prioriser la file d’attente avec l’équipe de soutien afin que les problèmes urgents soient réglés en premier, et maintenir l’arriéré et les délais de réponse dans les cibles convenues.
 Faire remonter les bogues aux équipes Produit et Développement avec des détails clairs et reproductibles, et en assurer le suivi jusqu’à leur résolution.
 Diriger les communications avec la clientèle lors de pannes, de versions problématiques ou d’autres escalades, et mener le suivi par la suite ou veiller à ce que l’équipe en assume la responsabilité de façon appropriée.
 Élaborer, en collaboration avec les développeurs et les responsables de produit, la base de connaissances, et créer et tenir à jour les guides d’exploitation internes et les modèles de réponse.
 Assumer la configuration de Jira Service Management, y compris les catégories, les flux de travail et les SLA.
 Collaborer avec l’équipe d’Intégration des clients pour assurer une transition fluide vers le soutien pour chaque nouveau client.
 Faire le suivi du rendement de l’équipe et des principaux facteurs du volume de billets, et en rendre compte au directeur général.
 Traiter les problèmes de soutien impliquant des clients par l’intermédiaire de leurs partenaires informatiques et des fournisseurs technologiques de Carrus.
 CE QUE NOUS RECHERCHONS 
 3 ans et plus d’expérience en soutien de logiciels B2B, dont au moins 2 ans à diriger ou à superviser officiellement une équipe de soutien.
 Un historique d’améliorations mesurables, comme la réduction de l’arriéré, l’augmentation de la satisfaction de la clientèle (CSAT) ou la diminution des billets récurrents.
 Maîtrise du français et de l’anglais, à l’écrit comme à l’oral.
 Expérience dans un environnement de soutien téléphonique ou de centre d’appels, en soutien de logiciels essentiels aux activités comme des systèmes ERP, de point de vente (PDV), de gestion des stocks ou de gestion de concessionnaires ou d’ateliers.
 Solides compétences pratiques en dépannage touchant les installations, les environnements hébergés, les autorisations des utilisateurs, le matériel de point de vente et les imprimantes, ainsi que les notions de base en réseautique.
 Expérience de la configuration et de la gestion d’une plateforme de billetterie comme Jira Service Management, Zendesk ou Freshdesk.
 Communication calme et claire, tant avec le personnel de comptoir mécontent qu’avec les propriétaires d’entreprise.
 Autonomie et capacité à diriger efficacement une équipe en télétravail.
 Atouts 
 Expérience dans le marché secondaire de l’automobile, par exemple dans la distribution de pièces, chez un distributeur-entrepositaire ou chez un fournisseur de systèmes de gestion d’ateliers (JMS).
 Connaissance des intégrations avec les fournisseurs, de l’EDI et des données de catalogues électroniques de pièces.
 Connaissances de base en SQL pour enquêter sur les problèmes de données.

 ABOUT CARRUS 
 Carrus builds the management software that auto parts distributors, wholesalers, and repair shops across Eastern Canada run their business on — from electronic parts catalogues and pricing to inventory, invoicing, and accounting.  You’ll find Carrus a great place to work if you want real ownership over how a team runs and work whose impact customers feel the same day. Carrus is part of Valsoft’s ecosystem of 150+ vertical software companies, giving you the stability and resources of one of Canada’s fastest-growing companies with the feel of a focused, close-knit team.
 THE ROLE 
 We’re looking for a bilingual Customer Support Lead to run Carrus’s support team day to day. If you enjoy solving problems with customers over the phone, coaching the people around you, and owning the results of a team, this is the right role for you.
 You’ll be responsible for autonomously improving upon our support system. You’ll work on identifying and implementing processes and workflow improvements to ensure team responsiveness and customer satisfaction, while also being encouraged to automate bottlenecks while maintaining service standards. You’ll be responsible for training and mentoring a customer service team, helping them improve and prioritize queues and workflows for seamless performance. You’ll learn our technology stack and build customer relations, being able to handle and resolve customer issues and escalations autonomously as well.

 WHAT YOU’LL DO 
 Develop and continuously improve the organization’s processes and workflows on managing support tickets, from collecting and tracking key data for KPIs, to the development of automation playbooks.
 Coach and mentor a team of support agents on best practices to increase ticket resolution rates and increase customer satisfaction.
 Lead the team day to day — ensure coverage during business hours, run daily huddles and one-on-ones, and set and model the standard for prompt, thorough resolution.
 Carry a share of the ticket queue, particularly on high-priority issues — take inbound calls and requests in French and English.
 Triage and prioritize the queue alongside the support team so urgent issues are resolved first and keep backlog and response times within agreed targets.
 Escalate bugs to Product and Development with clear, reproducible detail, and follow them through to resolution.
 Lead customer communication during outages, problem releases, or other escalations, and run the follow-up afterward or ensure appropriate ownership and accountability from the team.
 Co-develop the knowledge base alongside developers and product owners, and build and maintain internal runbooks and response templates.
 Own the configuration of Jira Service Management, including categories, workflows, and SLAs.
 Partner with Onboarding on a clean handoff to support for every new customer.
 Track and report team performance and the top drivers of ticket volume to the General Manager.
 Handle support-related issues involving customers through their IT partners and through Carrus’s technology vendors.
 WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR 
 3+ years in B2B software support, including at least 2 years formally leading or supervising a support team.
 A track record of measurable improvement, such as reducing backlog, raising CSAT, or cutting repeat tickets.
 Fluent in French and English, written and spoken.
 Experience in a phone-based or call-centre support environment, supporting business-critical software such as ERP, POS, inventory, or dealer/shop management systems.
 Strong hands-on troubleshooting across installs, hosted environments, user permissions, POS hardware and printers, and basic networking.
 Experience configuring and running a ticketing platform such as Jira Service Management, Zendesk, or Freshdesk.
 Calm, clear communication with both frustrated counter staff and business owners.
 Self-motivated and able to lead a team effectively in a remote environment.
 Nice to have 
 Experience in the automotive aftermarket, such as parts distribution, a warehouse distributor, or a JMS vendor.
 Familiarity with supplier integrations, EDI, and electronic parts catalogue data.
 Basic SQL for investigating data issues.

 - Stakeholder management and influence without authority across Product, Engineering, Sales, Customer Success, Support, Marketing, and Compliance, including driving durable alignment on difficult trade-offs

 - Clear written communication - your strategy docs and PRDs should require minimal interpretation

About the company 
 Mindrift connects specialists with project-based AI opportunities for leading tech companies, focused on testing, evaluating, and improving AI systems. This is a task-based, independent contractor opportunity, not an employment relationship. Participation is limited to this project.
 Project Highlights 
 Earnings per approved task: a fixed rate for each task, set in advance
 Fully self-scheduled: no minimum hours and no set schedule; you choose which tasks to take and when
 Remote: open to US-licensed physicians based in eligible US states
 No patient contact, no malpractice exposure: you review written clinical cases
 All contributors are license-verified physicians
 $50 one-time onboarding reward, paid once your first task on the project is approved
 What this project involves 
 We're looking for physicians (MD/DO) with an active, unrestricted US medical license to evaluate clinical EHR vignettes for a medical AI evaluation project. General and internal medicine are the main focus. Each task is a written clinical case, assessed against the project's acceptance criteria. Contributors may:
 Evaluate clinical EHR vignettes paired with a question, a proposed answer, and a distractor "trap" answer across diagnosis and treatment tasks, spanning cardiovascular, nervous, hematologic, respiratory, digestive, urinary, reproductive, musculoskeletal, and integumentary systems;
 Score the clinical reasoning quality of benchmark items: vignette accuracy and completeness, whether the vignette gives the answer away, answer correctness and gradeability, and trap quality;
 Check whether the reasoning chain reaches the answer from vignette facts alone, correct reasoning traces, and write short rationales.
 Each case receives three independent blind reads, followed by physician adjudication. Real clinical complexity only. You're improving the AI tools you'll eventually use yourself.
 What we look for 
 This project is a good fit for US-licensed physicians looking for a flexible, time-limited project they can fit around their other commitments. Ideally, contributors will have:
 Medical degree (MD or DO) and an active, unrestricted US medical license (verified at onboarding and re-checked monthly);
 Board certification or completed residency training, with direct patient care experience (attending-level preferred). Practising or retired physicians welcome;
 Broad, multi-system diagnostic and treatment experience (internal, family, emergency, or hospital medicine);
 Strong clinical reasoning: differential diagnosis, next-step management, and application of evidence-based guidelines;
 Prior experience in medical AI evaluation, clinical content or exam-question review, or medical annotation/QA (a plus);
 Strong written English (C1+).
 This project is not suitable for medical students, unlicensed medical graduates, non-physician clinicians (NPs, PAs, nurses, pharmacists), or non-clinical healthcare titles.
 How it works 
 Apply → Pass qualification(s) → Join the project → Complete tasks → Get paid for approved tasks
 Flexibility 
 You decide whether, when, and how much to contribute. There are no minimum hours, set schedules, or required availability. Task availability varies with project phases. Tasks are submitted through the platform and are approved when they meet the project’s acceptance criteria.
 Earnings 
 Earnings are paid only for completed and approved tasks. Each task type has a fixed rate. There is no time tracking and no hour logging. There are no tiers or speed adjustments to the rate. QA and adjudication tasks have a higher per-task rate.
 $50 one-time onboarding reward, paid once your first task on the project is approved.
 Quality incentives: additional earnings for high-quality approved tasks, on terms set out in the project guidelines.

The Company You’ll Join
 Carta is the connected platform and AI-native ecosystem for private capital. Built to replace fragmented tools with a single system of record, Carta brings together the software, services, and legal infrastructure that founders use to manage equity, fund managers use to run administration and reporting, and legal teams use to close transactions. Trusted by 55,000 companies and 1.8M+ equity holders in 160+ countries, and 10,000 funds and SPVs representing $250B+ in assets under management, Carta is transforming how private capital operates. Recognized by Fortune, Forbes, Fast Company, Inc. and Great Places to Work.
 For more information about our offices and culture, check out our Carta careers page .
 The Team You'll Work With 
 Every fund CFO’s office runs on spreadsheets, email threads, and a pile of portals that don’t talk to each other. We’re replacing all of it. Carta’s Investors business unit is building the system of record for private markets: the ledger, the books, the tax filings, the LP reporting, and the deal pipeline, all in one connected platform. Nearly 7,000 funds and SPVs and $150B in assets already run through it today.
 Here’s the fun part: we’re not building another portal. We’re building a programmable back office. An expense lands in an inbox and gets coded to the right entity and staged for approval. A capital call goes out from a sentence. A K-1 is ready on day one. The software does the work, and customers reach it through the AI tools they already use.
 It’s a pivotal moment for the business unit. The core is proven (90% of cash transactions reconciled in one day), and now we’re connecting it into a single platform that runs from fund financials to tax to LP reporting. You’ll join small, senior teams that blend startup-style speed with the rigor of software that moves real money.
 We’re hiring multiple engineers, and you’ll be hired into the Investors business unit as a whole, then matched to a focus area based on your strengths and interests during our interview process. These focus areas include:
 Fund Financials: Ledger, expense allocation, and cash reconciliation. Get the numbers right, automatically, at scale.
 Tax and Compliance: K-1s, KYC, and audit trails. Compliance as code instead of compliance as a checklist.
 LP Management and Reporting: Capital calls, distributions, PCAPs, and tearsheets. Turn quarterly reporting from a scramble into a query.
 The Problems You'll Solve 
 As a Staff Engineer, you are responsible for the long-term technical health and success of the Investors business unit. You’ll work to:
 Navigate Ambiguity: Tackle the most complex and poorly defined problems at Carta, breaking them down into navigable paths for the rest of the organization.
 Champion Systemic Improvement: Identify and eliminate failure patterns across multiple systems, driving architectural changes that improve scalability and reliability.
 Bridge Technical Gaps: Use your deep understanding of cross-functional domains to align multiple teams on major technical decisions.
 Define the AI Frontier: Lead the charge in transforming how we build by defining the context and building the rails that allow every person at Carta to leverage AI tools safely and effectively. You’ll help move the organization toward a future where AI amplifies our collective engineering impact.
 Uphold Engineering Standards: Set the vision for operational excellence and mentor senior engineers to raise the collective craft of the organization.
 About You 
 The Tech Stack: You are an expert in building distributed systems. While our primary stack is Python/Django, React, and Postgres, you should be comfortable guiding technical direction across JVM languages, gRPC, and cloud-native infrastructure (AWS). 
 Leadership: You lead through influence rather than authority, acting as a role model for constructive communication and technical discipline.
 Vision: You don't just solve the problem in front of you; you anticipate future roadblocks and build systems that support long-term business growth.
 Experience: We recommend 10+ years of professional software engineering experience with a track record of high-level technical leadership.
 Salary 
 Carta’s compensation package includes a market competitive salary, equity for all full time roles, exceptional benefits, and, for applicable roles, commissions plans. Our minimum cash compensation (salary + commission if applicable) range for this role is:
 $205,600 CAD - $257,000 CAD in Toronto, Ontario, Canada and Waterloo, Ontario, Canada
 Final offers may vary from the amount listed based on geography, candidate experience and expertise, and other factors.

GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.
 The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.
 * Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab. 
 An overview of this role
 As a Senior or Staff Backend Engineer with the Database Excellence group , you'll build and evolve database automation and PostgreSQL as a service capabilities for GitLab. The level will be determined during the hiring process. You'll use Go to automate the full lifecycle of PostgreSQL across GitLab's infrastructure, making database operations safer, more consistent, and easier to scale for databases that sit behind high-throughput, always-on internet services. You'll work closely with partner teams to shape how GitLab provisions and manages PostgreSQL in a fully remote, highly collaborative environment.
 Some examples of our projects:
 SQL Traffic Replay Tooling , which validates upgrades and changes against real production workloads.
 PostgreSQL as a Service Platform , which provides standardized, automated provisioning and lifecycle management for internal product databases.
 PostgreSQL Major Version Upgrade Automation , which supports safe, repeatable major upgrades at GitLab.com scale.
 What you’ll do
 Design, build, and maintain Go-based automation that manages the full PostgreSQL lifecycle, including provisioning, configuration, upgrades, failover, scaling, and decommissioning, reducing reactive operational work that currently takes more than 80% of the team's time.
 Build automation that works across infrastructure-as-code tooling and cloud infrastructure, and evaluate operator-based approaches as the platform evolves.
 Use AI agents as a regular part of building and operating services, including implementation, review, and reducing repetitive work, while keeping the context agents need in the repository so the whole team can build on it.
 Build for internet scale by designing automation and services for high-throughput, always-on production workloads, where GitLab.com traffic sets the bar for correctness, latency, and availability.
 Integrate compute, storage, networking, identity and access management, and managed data services across cloud providers into one coherent PostgreSQL platform instead of creating bespoke setups for each database.
 Build GitLab's PostgreSQL as a service platform to replace bespoke database setups with standardized, automated provisioning and lifecycle management, so supporting more databases doesn't require growing the operations team at the same rate.
 Collaborate closely with product management, infrastructure, software delivery, and other engineering teams to design and ship high-performing solutions.
 Research, design, and implement improvements to PostgreSQL performance, scalability, and data health, helping maintain more than 8 months of operational runway for all critical database saturation points.
 Review database automation and Go changes from other engineers and contributors, with attention to safety, maintainability, and performance.
 Document automation practices, PostgreSQL operational patterns, and guidance that helps engineers use and contribute to the platform.
 Build safe, repeatable automation for PostgreSQL major version upgrades at GitLab.com scale, validating changes against real production traffic before rollout.
 Operate what you build in production from end to end, using production feedback to guide each iteration.
 Take part in on-call or operational support where your team’s ownership model requires it.
 What you’ll bring
 Professional software engineering experience working with PostgreSQL in large, complex production environments, including experience building or operating a database-as-a-service product.
 Proficiency with Go, including designing, implementing, testing, and reviewing backend services.

Then you should consider joining Jobber! We’re looking for a Product Support Specialist to be part of our Customer Success department. This posting is for future opportunities on the team.

Jobber exists to help people in small businesses be successful. We work with small home service businesses, like your local plumbers, painters, and landscapers, to transform the way service is delivered through technology. With Jobber they can quote, schedule, invoice, and collect payments from their customers while providing an easy and professional customer experience. Running a small business today isn’t like it used to be—the way we consume and deliver service is changing rapidly, technology is evolving, and customers expect more. That’s why we put the power and flexibility in their hands to run their businesses how, where, and when they want! 

Our culture of transparency, inclusivity, collaboration, and innovation has been recognized by Great Place to Work, Canada’s Most Admired Corporate Cultures, and more. Jobber has also been named on the Globe and Mail’s Canada’s Top Growing Companies list, and Deloitte Canada’s Technology Fast 50™, Enterprise Fast 15, and Technology Fast 500™ lists. With an Executive team that has over thirty years of industry experience of leading the way, we’ve come a long way from our first customer in 2011—but we’ve just scratched the surface of what we want to accomplish for our customers https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EkfZmHrRLx4&list=PLoktA_D-2UEnxMLfCe93bANKXVXd2bdN8&index=24.

The team:

If our company values were a department, they would be the Customer Success department; they are humble, supportive, and truly give a sh*t about making sure our customers are successful in Jobber.  This group is one that cares about authentic interactions, empowering our customers, and providing top tier customer service. 

The role:

Our Product Support Specialists are the foundation to Jobber’s success. We have a strong focus on our customer, and this role will work with our hundreds of thousands of users to provide an award winning level of customer service. This is a dynamic, fast-paced contact centre environment—using live chat, phone or email, you will assist users in understanding the newest features, help with functionality and custom workflows, problem solve issues, or accept feedback. This role directly impacts the lives of our entrepreneurs who rely on Jobber to run their businesses, which is a responsibility we don’t take lightly. 

The Product Support Specialist will:

 - Respond to inquiries that encompass the entire Jobber ecosystem from new and existing customers through live chat, phone, or email.

 - Troubleshoot issues or problem solve questions that customers may have about a feature, bug, or work flow. 

 - Maintain high channel productivity across our different mediums.

 - Be a liaison for customer feedback to product and technical teams.

 - Build a knowledge base of FAQ’s and document all feedback and recommendations from our customers, ensuring the integrity of that data to help shape future decisions.

To be successful, you should:

 - Have 1 year of contact centre experience, preferred.

 - Be agile and adaptable to solve problems quickly. We’re growing fast and things are changing every day - both in our product and in our process. You need to be invigorated by this type of environment and be excited by a new challenge.

 - Be empathetic to our customers' journeys. Our biggest priority is to support our customers, so you need to be comfortable and confident diving into their issues and fill in your own knowledge gaps to better support them.

 - Be clear and effective in interactions with our customers over the phone. You should be confident in your verbal communication skills, being able to articulate information concisely and with a friendly demeanor will be crucial in addressing customer needs and resolving issues promptly.

 - Be able to craft professional and empathetic responses to customer inquiries via email and chat. Attention to detail and clarity in your writing will ensure our customers receive accurate and helpful information in every interaction.

 - Be curious. Asking questions and probing is essential in this role, and the key to being able to provide great customer service.

 - Be incredibly reliable for our customers and the rest of the success team. Being supportive is one of our company values, so showing up for your team and customers is number one. 

 - Be resilient in the face of adversity. Not every problem will be simple to solve and not every customer interaction will be a positive one. Being able to overcome those moments and learn from them for next time is key. 

 - Be confident with technology. You should be able to touch type to help you get through high-volume chats and be very comfortable navigating cloud-based software.

Please note: There are multiple different shifts for this team, in the application form you will select all the shifts you are open to:

 - Monday to Friday 5am-2pm MT (7am-4pm ET)

 - Monday to Friday 6am-3pm MT (8am-5pm ET)

 - Monday to Friday  7am-4pm MT (9am-6pm ET)

 - Monday to Friday 8am-5pm MT (10am-7pm ET)

 - Monday to Friday 9am-6pm MT (11am-8pm ET)

 - Monday to Friday 10am-7pm MT (12pm-9pm ET).

 - Monday to Friday 11am-8pm MT (1pm-10pm ET).

We believe great collaboration is intentional, and sometimes that means coming together in person to build, brainstorm, and connect. To support this, the role is open to candidates based in one of our hub cities: Edmonton, Toronto, Vancouver, or Kitchener-Waterloo.

Compensation:

At Jobber, we believe that compensation should be transparent, fair, and reflective of your experience and growth. This role has a minimum annual salary of $50,000, a midpoint of $58,800, and a maximum salary of $67,600, designed to show the progression from learning the ropes to truly excelling.

We design our compensation to reflect each new hire’s skills, experience against the complexity of the role, ensuring a fair and competitive salary. Our range is intentionally broad to support growth and long-term impact. The higher end of the range is reserved for those who have demonstrated deep expertise and lasting contributions, while offers between the minimum to the midpoint reflect strong potential with transferable work experience. This approach ensures that compensation aligns with both an individual’s current capabilities and their opportunity for future growth.

Base salary is just one part of a total compensation package that will include equity rewards, annual stipends for health and wellness, retirement savings matching, and an extended health package with fully paid premiums for body and mind. Your professional growth matters to us too! You’ll have access to a dedicated talent development program that includes career coaching and opportunities for career development.

We believe in transparency and open conversations about compensation. If you have any questions about our approach, we’re happy to discuss them throughout the hiring process!



The Interview Process: 

Step 1: We’ll review your application! The candidates whose customer service experience aligns with the role will be moved forward in the process. We're looking for problem solvers, and people used to working in a fast-paced and multi-tasking environment. Make sure to highlight this one your application!  

Step 2: AI interview! Candidates moving forward will receive a link to complete a brief, AI interview through Metaview.

Step 3: Initial convo with TA! A member of Talent Attraction will reach out to you for a first conversation. We want you to share your unique story and experience, and see how you’ll help drive us forward. This is also a great opportunity to ask questions about Jobber and the role! 

Step 4: Team Interviews!  You’ll have two interviews with your potential team leader and peers to dig into your previous experience and performance, as well as to see your skill set in action in a Customer Support role play. We’re constantly raising our bar and excited to see what you can bring to Jobber.

Step 5: Offer!

What you can expect from Jobber:

 - A total compensation package that includes an extended health benefits package with fully paid premiums for both body and mind, matching in RRSP, TFSA or FHSA, and stock options.

 - A dedicated Talent Development team and access to coaching, learning, and leadership programs to help you grow your career, reach your goals, and unlock your full potential.

 - A unique opportunity to build, grow, and leave your impact on a $400-billion industry that has no dominant player...yet.

 - To work with a group of people who are humble, supportive, and give a sh*t about our customers.

We believe that diverse teams perform better and that fostering an inclusive work environment is a key part of growing a successful team. We welcome people of diverse backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We are an equal opportunity employer, and we are committed to working with applicants requesting accommodation at any stage of the hiring process.



A bit more about us:

Job by job, we’re transforming the way service is delivered. Your lawn care provider, home cleaning service, plumber or painter could use Jobber to better connect with their customers, save time in the office, invoice faster, and get paid! We’re bringing tens of thousands of people together with technology to deliver billions of dollars a year in services to happy customers. Jobber exists to help make these small businesses successful, and when they’re successful we all win!
